headline: Fewer deliveries and thinner margins pressure the quarter
summary_short: Toll Brothers' fiscal Q2 2026 revenue fell 7.6% y/y to $2.53 billion as home deliveries dropped 14% on a smaller entering backlog, while net income fell 26% to $260.6 million on margin compression and a swing to a loss from unconsolidated joint ventures.
summary_long: Home sales gross margin fell to 23.9% from 26.0% on higher incentives and inventory impairments; SG&A rose to 10.3% of home sales revenue on higher payroll costs. Diluted EPS fell 22% to $2.72. Income from unconsolidated entities swung to a $16.7 million loss (from $11.5 million income) as a prior-year JV gain didn't recur and new JV impairment charges of $13.5 million hit the quarter. Backlog fell 8% to $6.32 billion as spec homes, built and delivered faster, took a larger share of contracts. Selling communities rose to 459 from 421. Cash rose to $1.11 billion, aided by ~$330 million from the Kennedy Wilson Apartment Living sale. No numeric guidance given; quarterly dividend raised to $0.26/share.

drivers.explanation: Revenue and profit fell y/y as a 14% drop in home deliveries and margin compression from higher incentives/impairments outweighed an 8% higher average delivered price, plus a swing to a JV loss.
Decrease attributable to a 14% decrease in homes delivered, offset in part by an 8% increase in average delivered price; fewer deliveries reflect a smaller starting backlog and fewer spec homes.
Increase in cost of revenues as a percentage of home sales revenue was principally due to an increase in sales incentives and higher inventory impairment charges.
Dollar increase in SG&A was due primarily to higher payroll costs, offset in part by reduced commissions and advertising spend.
Beyond lower revenue and thinner margins, income from unconsolidated entities swung to a $16.7M loss as a $15.5M prior-year JV gain didn't recur and new $13.5M JV impairment charges hit this quarter.
Decrease primarily due to a smaller number of homes in backlog at fiscal-year start versus a year earlier and fewer spec home deliveries, offset in part by faster construction cycle times.
11% fewer homes in backlog as spec homes — built and delivered within a quarter rather than sitting in backlog — took a larger share of signed contracts and deliveries.
Filing does not tie a single cause to the cash balance; the six-month period included ~$330M of net cash proceeds from the Kennedy Wilson Apartment Living portfolio sale.
